title: Grafana 9.4 proxy issue (Cloudflare)
body:
<!--
Please use this template to create your bug report. By providing as much info as possible you help us understand the issue, reproduce it and resolve it for you quicker. Therefore take a couple of extra minutes to make sure you have provided all info needed.

PROTIP: record your screen and attach it as a gif to showcase the issue.

- Questions should be posted to: https://<redacted-host>
- Use query inspector to troubleshoot issues: https://bit.ly/2XNF6YS
- How to record and attach gif: https://bit.ly/2Mi8T6K
-->

**What happened**:
Running a simple Grafana instane in a Docker on Ubuntu 22.04
Protected by Cloudflare Tunnel
Upgraded grafana from 9.3 to 9.4
Grafana doesn't load anymore, shows an error page:
"If you're seeing this Grafana has failed to load its application files"

**What you expected to happen**:
Grafana to load

It does load via the direct IP+port internally, so I understand one would think that Cloudflare is the issue, however the upgrade is the thing that breaks it, so I am looking for the breaking change and how to reconfigure Cloudflare if needed.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Deploy standard cloudflare tunnel
Deploy docker container for grafana 9.4

If i revert the image to 9.3 it works perfectly.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Grafana version: 9.4
- Data source type & version: 
- OS Grafana is installed on: Ubuntu LTS 22.04
- User OS & Browser: Firefox  110
- Grafana plugins: none
- Others:

I can confirm this.
It happens with 9.4.0-Beta Release and also the 9.4.1 release (this looks for me like a "broken" versioning that the jump happened to 9.4.1).

I had to roll back to 9.3.6 otherwise it was not possible to use Grafana with cloudflare.

comments.body:
I can confirm that the following actions result in a working Grafana  v9.4.3 (cf0a135595) installation with CloudFlare protection again:

1. Deploy latest image
2. Go to CF dashboard, https://dash.cloudflare.com, go to Speed, Optimization, uncheck "JavaScript" in Minify section
3. Go to the dashboard of CF again, open your site/domain, click on Caching, Configuration, perform a Complete Purge
4. Open Firefox and clear all data https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/clear-cookies-and-site-data-firefox for the Grafana site you are working with

I will leave the debate on "where this should be fixed" to the SME's.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body: > Even if you minify an already minified file it should still be valid as long as the original final is valid. Whilst I appreciate that up until recently Grafana has worked with Cloudflare's Auto Minify feature we have never officially supported it. Auto Minify operates by automatically modifying the source code of a website by not only minifying but also stripping "unnecessary characters from HTML, JavaScript, and CSS files". I would expect this to cause issues with already minified code as the "auto minifier" will likely make assumptions of the code passed into it. I believe this is why the feature has the following disclaimer: _Note: Please note that this feature may not be fully compatible with certain newer CSS and JS language features, which could potentially affect the functionality of your site._ > Do you think is worth it to track down the source of the problem. In regard to this specific issue it appears something in the vendors chunk is conflicting with auto minify. This chunk contains most of the 3rd party NPM package code that Grafana depends on to function and regularly receives updates which could at any time cause Auto Minify to fail. There is a [similar issue](https:///t/minification-produces-invalid-javascript/406236) reported on the Cloudflare community forums which might help shed some light on this type of issue. I would suggest opening a bug report with Cloudflare and point them at the offending file. Furthermore if we were to enable integrity checks (SRI) on Grafana’s script files or rely on HTML comments for a some sort of functionality in the future I'm pretty sure the Auto Minify feature will cause things to fail. Since CloudFlare has configuration / page rules to disable auto minify for a certain path and Grafana assets are already minified you should not see any difference and anything else that is behind CloudFlare will get minified as before. Make sure to purge the cache of the specific file that is causing the issue after creating the rule.
